approval.note: Approved mTORC1 inhibitor with genuine pediatric indications (TSC-SEGA >=1y, TSC partial-onset seizures >=2y, oral suspension). The only candidate with an approved pediatric oncology-adjacent indication in a tumour-predisposition syndrome (TSC).

claims.text: Same senomorphic mechanism as sirolimus: mTORC1 inhibition blunts the pro-inflammatory SASP via translational control of IL1A and MAPKAPK2, dampening senescent-cell paracrine damage without killing the cells.

Pediatric tumour-predisposition precedent: in the phase 3 EXIST-1 trial, everolimus produced significant SEGA volume reductions versus placebo in children/adults with tuberous sclerosis complex - proof that chronic mTOR inhibition is tolerated and effective in a paediatric cancer-predisposition population.

Label-reported pediatric tolerability (openFDA set_id 01f7b5fb; the EXIST-1 primary trial is PMID:23158522, whose own exposure was ~1 year): in EXIST-1/Study 2485 open-label follow-up (115 pediatric patients, median 4.1 years exposure), everolimus did not appear to adversely impact growth and pubertal development - the key reassurance for use in a growth-restricted child, tempered by higher infection rates in patients <6 years (96% any infection, 35% serious infection).
claims.note: Growth/puberty statement is from the FDA label pediatric_use text (set_id in approval block), summarised here as a label fact.

claims.text: Genotype-specific hook shared with sirolimus: mTORC1 hyperactivity correlates with sarcopenia predisposition in monoallelic BubR1-mutant MVA mice.

Counter-consideration: as with all mTOR inhibitors, immunosuppression reduces tumour immune surveillance; everolimus additionally carries renal-failure and metabolic warnings relevant to a child with nephrocalcinosis, and label advises completing childhood vaccinations before starting treatment.
claims.note: Renal/metabolic/infection warnings are label facts (set_id in approval block); the immune-surveillance reasoning is ours.

pediatric.label_source: openFDA drug/label set_id 01f7b5fb-be0d-4adf-acd2-6899018de966 (effective 2025-09-05); everolimus tablets and tablets for oral suspension
pediatric.approved_pediatric_indication: TSC-associated SEGA requiring intervention: patients >=1 year. Adjunctive treatment of TSC-associated partial-onset seizures: >=2 years (oral suspension). (Quoted label facts.)
pediatric.label_pediatric_dosing_fact: TSC-SEGA: 4.5 mg/m2 once daily titrated to trough 5-15 ng/mL; TSC partial-onset seizures: 5 mg/m2 once daily, trough 5-15 ng/mL (quoted label facts, not advice).
key_risks: Infections, including serious infections, at higher frequency under age 6 (label: 96% any infection vs 67% in >=6y; 35% serious vs 7%) - immunosuppression concern in a cancer-predisposed child.

Non-infectious pneumonitis, stomatitis, renal failure (monitor renal function - nephrocalcinosis phenotype), hyperglycaemia/hyperlipidaemia, myelosuppression, impaired wound healing, radiation sensitisation, embryo-fetal toxicity, live-vaccine avoidance.
No boxed warning on this oncology label, unlike sirolimus's transplant boxed warning - but the same class-level immunosuppression applies.
monitoring: Trough concentrations (5-15 ng/mL target in labeled uses)
Infection surveillance; complete childhood vaccinations before initiation (label advice); no live vaccines

celegans.expected: as sirolimus; mTOR-pathway conservation makes worm a plausible pharmacodynamic model

fibroblasts.assay: everolimus exposure on MVA patient fibroblasts
fibroblasts.readout: SASP cytokines, p-S6, aneuploidy rate, BubR1 level, growth rate
fibroblasts.expected: SASP suppression; confirm no increase in aneuploidy or growth suppression

verdict_reason: Preferred mTOR-axis candidate over sirolimus for this child: it has real approved pediatric indications in a tumour-predisposition syndrome (TSC-SEGA >=1y; TSC seizures >=2y) with label-reported absence of growth/puberty harm over ~4 years (PMID:23158522 context), where sirolimus has no pediatric approval below 13 and a malignancy boxed warning. Same senomorphic mechanism (PMID:26147250) and the same genotype-specific mTORC1-hyperactivity hook (PMID:31738183). Residual concerns: immunosuppression in a cancer-predisposed child, renal function monitoring given nephrocalcinosis, and higher infection rates under age 6.
